result_text:
Any folder whose name starts with `mock` or `__mock` is now classified as test code, whatever the rest of its name is. That covers plain `mock/`, `mock.data/`, `mock(old)/`, `mock-größe/` and `mock模拟/`.

The change is in `ScopingConventions.java`, in `addMockResourcesConventions()`. The two patterns `.*/__mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*` and `.*/mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*` became `.*/__mock[^/]*/.*` and `.*/mock[^/]*/.*`. The old ones required at least one character from a limited ASCII set after `mock`, which is why those three kinds of folder slipped through.

The match stays inside one folder name. `remock/` and `demo/` don't match because the pattern needs `/mock` at the start of a folder name. Files named `mock.java` or `mockery.java` don't match because the pattern needs a `/` after the folder name.

Backslash paths are already handled by `SourceFileFilter.pathMatches`, which also tries the pattern against the path with `\` turned into `/`, so I changed nothing there.

I ran the `Scoping*` tests in `codeanalyzer`; they pass. I didn't add test cases for the new folder names or run the old folders (`mocks/`, `__mocks__/`, `mock-data/` and so on) against the new patterns, though the new patterns accept everything the old ones did. Nothing is committed.
